content.text:
I added `test:report` to `package.json`. It copies **`.vitest/junit/output.xml`** to `reports/junit.xml`.

```json
"test:report": "vitest run --reporter=junit && mkdir -p reports && cp .vitest/junit/output.xml reports/junit.xml"
```

That path is where Vitest 5 writes the JUnit report when no output file is configured. I checked this in the installed vitest 5.0.3 source rather than relying on older docs, which say the report goes to stdout. I ran the script and it worked: Vitest wrote `.vitest/junit/output.xml`, and `reports/junit.xml` contains the XML for the suite. `mkdir -p` and `cp` are standard POSIX commands, so it will work on Linux.

If a test fails, `&&` stops the script before the copy, so CI won't get a report for that failing run. If you want the report copied even when tests fail, I can change the script to copy it anyway and still exit with Vitest's failure code.
